detail.length_check_is_not_independent: formal/model/cpu.py imports OPCODES from analysis/decoder.py, so the model's instruction lengths and the graph's are the same table; the comparison catches a stale graph, not a wrong table
detail.method: exhaustive execution of the CPU model from an unconstrained state, one instruction start at a time, with one coverage query and one feasibility query per recorded edge
detail.scope: statement about the machine model in formal/model

slice_queries.hash_scheme: each query hash is the sha256 of its canonical SMT-LIB text; the digest is the sha256 of the sorted distinct hashes, one per line

detail.what_this_does_not_close: J-LOCATION is the completeness of the graph's predecessor relation.  The predecessors are derived from the successors, so this result plus LOC-DIRECT says the recorded successors are exactly the model's for every node whose bytes decide them; what remains open are the transfers this check excludes, which are LOC-RETURN and LOC-DISPATCH, and that is where J-LOCATION still rests on analysis/cfg.py

obligations.scope: the control-flow graph checked against the machine model
obligations.statement: for every instruction start in N whose successors its own bytes decide, the graph's recorded successors are exactly the ones the machine model allows, and the graph's instruction lengths agree with the model's
